## Bucket insert contracts

Inquiry and time request attachments use signed upload URLs issued by the owning
web API with `createDynamicAdminClient`. Browser uploads consume those tickets;
direct authenticated SQL inserts are not their supported upload contract.
`POST /api/reports/upload-url` issues inquiry tickets and
`POST /api/v1/workspaces/[wsId]/time-tracking/requests/upload-url` issues time
request tickets. Neither requires authenticated SELECT grants on the underlying
inquiry or private time request tables.

Client (anon and authenticated) inserts are limited to the `workspaces` bucket
by a restrictive policy, and bucket creation is server-only. The legacy inquiry
INSERT policy and the root-workspace changelog upload, update and delete
policies are dropped, so client uploads to the changelog and inquiry buckets are
denied; inquiry uploads go through the server (service role) or issued tickets.
Avatars and banners use server-issued tickets; artifact buckets remain
server-owned. Regression coverage:
`apps/database/supabase/tests/storage-insert-policies.sql`.

## Access model

The `workspaces` bucket stores objects as `<wsId>/<root>/...`. Supabase Storage
enforces `storage.objects` RLS for browser and user-token clients. Owning server
APIs use the service role, which bypasses RLS. Migration
`20261026170000_least_privilege_workspace_storage_rls.sql` replaced the original
policies. Those let any workspace member read, write and delete every object.
`20261026192000_topic_announcements_private_storage_root.sql` added
`topic-announcements/**` to the private roots.

All rules require a `MEMBER` workspace membership; guests are excluded.
`workspace_storage.object_access(name, operation, actor)` evaluates them. The
`workspace_storage` schema is not exposed through PostgREST, so clients cannot
call the helper with a forged actor:

| Root | select | insert / update | delete |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chat/<chatId>/**` (legacy AI attachments) | chat creator | none | chat creator |
| `chats/ai/resources/<chatId>/**` | chat creator | none | chat creator |
| `chats/ai/resources/temp/<userId>/**` | that user | none | that user |
| other `chats/**` (native Chat), `external-apps/**`, `AI Agent Imports/**`, `mira/images/**`, `recordings/**`, `topic-announcements/**`, `.tuturuuu/**` | none | none | none |
| `project-updates/**` | member | member | member |
| `template-backgrounds/**` | member | `manage_drive` | `manage_drive` |
| everything else, including root-level files (Drive) | `view_drive`, `manage_drive` or `admin` | `manage_drive` or `admin` | `manage_drive` or `admin` |

Workspace creators count as `admin`, which mirrors `has_workspace_permission`.

- Private roots match case-insensitively and never fall back to Drive permissions.
  `AI Agent Imports` contains spaces; the match uses the literal segment.
  `drive/mira/qr/**` (QR codes saved to Drive) stays a Drive object; only
  `mira/images/**` is private.
- Names containing empty, `.` or `..` segments are denied.
- Clients cannot write private roots. Chat uploads use
  `POST /api/ai/chat/upload-url`, which checks membership and chat ownership
  before it issues a signed upload URL. An existing chat must belong to the
  caller. An id that does not exist yet is allowed for draft attachments.
  Uploads never overwrite (`upsert: false`), and Supabase signed upload tokens
  have a fixed 2-hour lifetime.
- `POST /api/ai/chat/delete-file` accepts only the caller's own temp folder or
  an existing chat (UUID segment) the caller created. Orphaned and non-chat
  folders are not deletable through it.
- Topic announcement attachments (`topic-announcements/attachments/**`) upload
  through `POST /api/v1/workspaces/[wsId]/storage/upload-url`. Its topic branch
  checks `ENABLE_TOPIC_ANNOUNCEMENTS` and `manage_users` before it issues a
  signed upload URL, and it is the only Drive route that accepts the root.
  Email delivery downloads attachments with the service role. Neither
  `view_drive` nor `manage_drive` grants direct or Drive-route access.
- Meeting recording routes check membership and the recording session, then use
  the service role for storage. Playback signs only paths inside the verified
  session folder.
- `project-updates` keeps member access because its task route still uses a
  request-scoped client. Move it to a service-role route before tightening it.
- The private-root list follows the Drive private upload census in
  [Drive](/platform/applications/drive). Add new private roots to the helper,
  the Drive path policy and the test matrix together.

RESTRICTIVE `workspace_storage_guard_*` policies enforce the same helper on every
command. The legacy `Enable insert for authenticated users only` policy
(`WITH CHECK (true)`) can no longer widen access to this bucket. Before this
migration, it let non-members insert into any workspace folder.

## Performance

`workspace_storage.actor_access()` resolves the caller's member, view and manage
workspace sets once per statement. Policies pass it as
`(select workspace_storage.actor_access())`, which runs as an InitPlan. Each row
then costs path parsing and array lookups, plus one primary-key probe on
`ai_chats` for chat attachment rows. Private roots are denied before any table
lookup. Guards use `CASE` so the bucket check runs first and other buckets never
call the helper.

Measured on a disposable local stack listing one Drive folder of 20,000 objects
as a `view_drive` member (median of 5 runs):

| Policy set | `count(*)` of the folder | `storage.search` first page (100) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2023 member-wide policies | 111 ms | 120 ms |
| First path-scoped version (per-row permission calls) | 1,493 ms | 1,557 ms |
| Current path-scoped version | 174 ms | 183 ms |
| Incident rollback variant | 248 ms | 256 ms |

## Regression coverage

`apps/database/supabase/tests/workspace-storage-least-privilege-rls.sql` covers
15 objects across every root. Each is probed by a non-member, a member, a
`view_drive` viewer, a `manage_drive` manager, the chat owner/uploader and
`service_role`, for select/insert/update/delete. With 10 structural checks
(including the workspace creator and the MEMBER default `admin` paths), that
is 370 assertions. Each probe runs in a rolled-back subtransaction.

Route tests in `apps/web/src/__tests__/mind-chat-file-app-session-route.test.ts`
cover the upload-url and delete-file ownership checks, including missing-chat
and non-UUID delete rejection.

## Verify on a disposable stack

Run this on a remote devbox only, never on the shared laptop. Copy
`apps/database/supabase` to a scratch directory and give `config.toml` a unique
`project_id` and free ports. Then, from `apps/database`:

```bash
ttr resources run -- node scripts/run-supabase.js --workdir "$SCRATCH" start
ttr resources run -- node scripts/run-supabase.js --workdir "$SCRATCH" \
  test db supabase/tests/workspace-storage-least-privilege-rls.sql
```

Stop it afterwards with `stop --project-id <id> --no-backup`.

## Rollback

There are two rollbacks in `apps/database/rollbacks/`. Each is one transaction,
does not touch objects, and can run from the forward state or from the other
rollback's state. Re-applying the forward migration body also removes either
rollback's policies.

- **Incident (preferred):**
  `20261026170000_least_privilege_workspace_storage_rls.incident-rollback.sql`.
  Members regain 2023-style access to non-private objects, with no `view_drive`
  check.
  - Private roots stay service-role only.
  - RESTRICTIVE insert and update guards keep the legacy `WITH CHECK (true)`
    policy from letting non-members write.
  - It is plain SQL and drops the helpers.
  - Proof: `apps/database/verification/workspace-storage-rls-incident-rollback.sql`
    (14 assertions).
- **Topic announcements root:**
  `20261026192000_topic_announcements_private_storage_root.rollback.sql`
  restores the 20261026170000 `object_access` body, returning
  `topic-announcements/**` to Drive permissions. It reopens that MEDIUM finding.
  Run it before either 20261026170000 rollback when unwinding both.
- **Faithful:** `20261026170000_least_privilege_workspace_storage_rls.rollback.sql`.
  It restores the exact 20231004102905 policies.
  - This reopens the HIGH finding and non-member inserts.
  - Use it only when exact prior behaviour is required.
  - Proof: `apps/database/verification/workspace-storage-rls-rollback-roundtrip.sql`
    (7 assertions).

To prove a round trip on the disposable stack:

1. Apply the rollback with `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1`.
2. Run its verification file.
3. Re-apply the forward migration file.
4. Re-run the 370-assertion test.

The migration runs inside an explicit `begin`/`commit` with
`set local lock_timeout = '5s'` and `statement_timeout = '30s'`. Its policy DDL
needs a brief `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock on `storage.objects`. On the disposable
stack, with another session holding `ACCESS SHARE` on the table, the migration
failed after 5 seconds with `canceling statement due to lock timeout` and left
no partial changes (no schema, the policies unchanged). Retry it when that
happens.
